claims.text: Edge video detection wastes energy on redundant frames.
claims.poster_quote: Edge video detection wastes energy on redundant frames.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Video object detection on edge devices requires running computationally expensive detectors over long frame streams, leading to high energy consumption and sustained GPU utilization.
claims.reason: Section I, first paragraph, explicitly states that video object detection on edge devices leads to high energy consumption due to computationally expensive detectors running over long frame streams.

claims.text: FixedSkip hurts accuracy during motion.
claims.poster_quote: FixedSkip hurts accuracy during motion.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Fixed-cadence skipping (the simplest content-blind baseline studied in prior work [22]–[24]) drops accuracy sharply: on the BDD100K MOT [11], skipping every second frame loses 8.6 pp AP@50 (average precision at IoU 0.5; 14% relative), and skipping four out of every five frames loses 28.8 pp (47%). A fixed schedule cannot detect when a new object enters the frame, when an occlusion clears, or when an object accelerates.
claims.reason: Section I, paragraph 5, explains that FixedSkip strategies are content-blind and result in significant accuracy loss during motion, supporting the claim.

claims.text: ALBIREO skips frames adaptively without retraining or codec assumptions.
claims.poster_quote: ALBIREO skips frames adaptively without retraining or codec assumptions.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: We present A LBIREO, a detector-agnostic, codec-free, adaptive inference framework that wraps off-the-shelf object detectors and decides when detector invocation can be safely skipped based on scene content and per-object temporal state. A LBIREO requires no detector modification or detector retraining and is designed as a drop-in efficiency layer for improving the accuracy–energy–latency tradeoff of edge video-detection pipelines.
claims.reason: Section I, paragraph 2, explicitly describes ALBIREO as an adaptive inference framework that skips frames without requiring detector retraining or codec assumptions.

claims.text: On BDD100K with YOLO26x, ALBIREO cuts energy 17.6% on Thor.
claims.poster_quote: On BDD100K with YOLO26x, ALBIREO cuts energy 17.6% on Thor,
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: On the primary YOLO26x configuration, A LBIREO improves AP@50 by +0.8 pp while reducing energy by 17.6% on Thor and 14.4% on Orin.
claims.reason: Section I, paragraph 6, explicitly states that ALBIREO reduces energy by 17.6% on Thor with YOLO26x on BDD100K.

claims.text: On BDD100K with YOLO26x, ALBIREO boosts AP@50 by +0.8 pp.

claims.text: ALBIREO dominates the Pareto frontier.
claims.poster_quote: On BDD100K with YOLO26x, ALBIREO cuts energy 17.6% on Thor, boosts AP@50 by +0.8 pp, and dominates the Pareto frontier.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Sweeping the primary uncertainty threshold on YOLO26x traces an AP@50–EDP Pareto frontier that dominates the evaluated frame-skipping baselines (FixedSkip-N , CTD, Statues) within the target operating region (AP@50 ≥ 0.50).

claims.text: ALBIREO maintains AP@50 within ±1.2 pp of per-frame inference across detectors while reducing energy 12.1–17.6%.
claims.poster_quote: It maintains AP@50 within ±1.2 pp of per-frame inference across detectors while reducing energy 12.1–17.6%.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Across all evaluated detectors and platforms, A LBIREO keeps AP@50 within 1.2 pp of Vanilla per-frame inference while reducing energy by 12.1–17.6%.
claims.reason: Section I, paragraph 6, explicitly states that ALBIREO maintains AP@50 within ±1.2 pp of per-frame inference while reducing energy by 12.1–17.6% across detectors.

claims.text: Energy savings persist across power modes (15W–120W).
claims.poster_quote: Energy savings persist across power modes (15W–120W).
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Total energy savings stay within 15.3–17.7% across a 4.6× power-budget spread, and are largest at Orin’s strict 15 W budget.
claims.reason: Section IV-D, Table V, and accompanying text confirm that energy savings persist across power modes (15W–120W).

claims.text: Uncertainty trigger (covariance growth) outperforms CTD’s stale-reference trigger.
claims.poster_quote: Uncertainty trigger (covariance growth) outperforms CTD’s stale-reference trigger.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: CTD uses a Mahalanobis-distance score relative to the most recent detection; as consecutive skips accumulate, that reference becomes stale. A LBIREO instead gates inference using covariance growth from the current object state, so the trigger directly reflects how long the state has evolved without measurement.
claims.reason: Section V-A, Versus CTD, explains that ALBIREO’s uncertainty trigger outperforms CTD’s stale-reference trigger by using covariance growth as a forward-looking signal.

claims.text: Rescue handles detector flicker, crucial for maintaining AP@50.
claims.poster_quote: Rescue handles detector flicker, crucial for maintaining AP@50.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The no-rescue variants cluster between 0.572 and 0.578 AP@50, while rescue increases AP@50 to 0.617. Thus, among these components, rescue is the largest contributor to AP@50.
claims.reason: Section IV-F, Table VI, and accompanying text confirm that rescue is crucial for maintaining AP@50.

claims.text: Empty-scene screening is effective only when conditionally applied.
claims.poster_quote: Empty-scene screening is effective only when conditionally applied.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: ERD-only runs the empty-road classifier of Liu and Kang [45] on every frame and skips detection when the scene is classified empty, with no Kalman tracking. Even with the same BDD100K-fine-tuned ERD used by A LBIREO, running ERD on every frame yields a 7.6% skip rate, though per-clip energy increases by 28% and the average frame time grows by 134% on Thor. The reason is straightforward: the ERD CNN runs on all frames, and the full detector still runs on the ∼92% classified as non-empty.
claims.reason: Section IV-C explains that empty-scene screening is effective only when conditionally applied, as running ERD on every frame increases energy and frame time.

claims.text: CPU overhead is platform-dependent (visible on Orin, negligible on Thor).
claims.poster_quote: CPU overhead is platform-dependent (visible on Orin, negligible on Thor) but GPU savings dominate.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: On Orin, average CPU power roughly doubles under A LBIREO from 1.6 W to 3.6 W, while CPU utilization rises from ∼7% to ∼23%. This increase comes from A LBIREO’s per-frame bookkeeping: Kalman prediction, two-stage IoU/Mahalanobis matching, and rescue accounting run on the CPU, regardless of whether detector inference is triggered. On Thor’s larger fourteen-core Neoverse V3AE CPU complex, the same operations do not increase CPU power measurably.
claims.reason: Section IV-G confirms that CPU overhead is platform-dependent, visible on Orin but negligible on Thor.

claims.text: GPU savings dominate over CPU overhead.
claims.poster_quote: CPU overhead is platform-dependent (visible on Orin, negligible on Thor) but GPU savings dominate.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: GPU energy drops by 17.5% on Thor and 19.0% on Orin, exceeding the total-energy reduction. CPU and IO/MEM changes are smaller and platform-dependent.
claims.reason: Section IV-G confirms that GPU savings dominate over CPU overhead.

claims.text: Per-clip analysis shows ALBIREO adapts to content: dense scenes use rescue for accuracy, sparse scenes save energy via empty-frame skipping.
claims.poster_quote: Per-clip analysis shows ALBIREO adapts to content: dense scenes use rescue for accuracy, sparse scenes save energy via empty-frame skipping.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: On a dense urban clip (no empty frames; 96% AI rate), A LBIREO and Vanilla draw similar power because the detector runs on most frames; rescue primarily preserves AP@50 rather than reducing energy. On a sparse highway clip (69% E, 4% AI), A LBIREO’s GPU power drops sharply during long ERD-only stretches, while Vanilla continues running full detector inference.
claims.reason: Section IV-H and Figure 7 show that ALBIREO adapts to content, using rescue for accuracy in dense scenes and empty-frame skipping for energy savings in sparse scenes.

claims.text: Skip rates are 19–22% across detectors.
claims.poster_quote: Skip rates: 19–22% across detectors
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The frame-state breakdown highlights two important behaviors. First, the total skip rate E + P is 19.3% for YOLO26x, 21.3% for YOLO11x, and 22.2% for RF-DETR.
claims.reason: Section IV-E confirms that skip rates are 19–22% across detectors.

claims.label: supported

claims.poster_quote: Rescue alone lifts AP@50 from 0.572–0.578 to 0.617
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The no-rescue variants cluster between 0.572 and 0.578 AP@50, while rescue increases AP@50 to 0.617.

claims.poster_quote: ALBIREO wraps detectors with three mechanisms: uncertainty trigger, flicker rescue, and empty-scene screen.

claims.poster_quote: All run online, no detector changes needed.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: A LBIREO targets causal, online, single-stream edge inference: every decision uses only the current frame and state carried from earlier frames, and future frames are never accessed.

claims.text: ALBIREO uses Kalman filters to skip when prediction covariance < threshold u.
claims.poster_quote: Uses Kalman filters to skip when prediction covariance < threshold u
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: A LBIREO uses the projected covariance trace as its uncertainty signal: τ = tr HP H ⊤ . Predict steps increase τ because no new detector measurement has constrained the object state... A LBIREO skips detector invocation when all active object states satisfy τ < u.
claims.reason: Section III-A explicitly describes how ALBIREO uses Kalman filters to skip when prediction covariance < threshold u.

claims.text: Rescue emits predicted boxes during brief detector misses.
claims.poster_quote: Rescue emits predicted boxes during brief detector misses
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: A rescued state emits its Kalman-predicted bounding box for the current frame, but it does not receive a Kalman update because no real detector measurement was observed.

claims.paper_evidence: When no active object states exist, the uncertainty trigger has no per-object covariance to consult... A LBIREO instead uses a lightweight binary scene classifier, the empty-road detector (ERD), to decide whether full detection is needed.

claims.text: ALBIREO has limitations: drift under erratic motion and domain-dependent empty-scene classifier.
claims.poster_quote: Limitations: drift under erratic motion, domain-dependent empty-scene classifier
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Three limitations of the current design point to natural extensions. First, the constant-acceleration Kalman dynamics fit many vehicle-dominated dashcam scenes, but can drift under highly erratic motion, such as a pedestrian making an abrupt lateral move at a crosswalk. Second, the empty-scene screen is domain-dependent. In this paper, ERD is fine-tuned for BDD100K dashcam scenes, which is appropriate for our evaluation, but not automatically transferable to other camera domains such as indoor surveillance, aerial video, or robot-mounted cameras.
claims.reason: Section V-D explicitly discusses ALBIREO’s limitations, including drift under erratic motion and the domain-dependent empty-scene classifier.
